approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local graph genetic algorithm whose oracle budget is spent by a Gaussian-process Thompson sampler, with one stagnation reflex added by the Child that became this Anchor. It keeps every molecule scored in the current session in a chronological archive and the best sixty-four in a breeding population, draws breeding parents from high-scoring score quantiles, and builds a fresh field of a hundred and sixty de novo offspring for each announced batch of ten, either by connected-fragment crossover of two parents with an optional finishing edit or by a short random walk of atom, bond and ring edits on one parent, discarding anything that is not a single ordinary connected graph, is already known in this session, or introduces a sulfur environment outside a fixed neutral envelope more often than its own scored parents did. It then fits one Gaussian process to the accepted scores of this session alone - integer-count radius-two Morgan fingerprints, a generalized Tanimoto kernel, unit prior amplitude, a fixed small observation noise, and labels recentred and rescaled by the archive's own running mean and spread - and draws one correlated posterior sample per batch position over the whole field. The ten molecules sent to the oracle are the sequential maxima of those draws, each winner removed before the next position, so a candidate the model rates poorly on average can still win a position when its sampled residual is large. The reflex added on top is a single counter of consecutive announced batches that failed to raise the session's best score: while it stands at three or more, only the forty highest posterior means of the unchanged field are eligible, and the first improving batch restores the full field. Everything this algorithm believes about chemistry therefore passes through one location and one scale, fitted to the whole archive at once.
approach.novelty: This node replaces that single predictor by a mixture of the same Gaussian processes whose number of components and membership are inferred online from this session's own accepted records, so the archive may contain several regions that behave differently instead of one smooth surface. Each component carries its own location and its own scale, estimated from its own members; a candidate is priced mainly by the component that actually knows it rather than by the whole archive at once; and the uncertainty the sampler consumes is the sum of two parts - how unsure the responsible components are about this candidate, and how much the components disagree with each other about it. A molecule unlike anything the session has accepted falls back on a fresh, empty component and is priced at the prior spread instead of being pulled onto the archive mean with a small residual. The sampling law is deliberately untouched: the same joint draw with the same correlated residuals, one array of random numbers per batch consumed in the same order, the same sequential maxima with each winner removed, and the same stall reflex, now reading the new posterior mean. That boundary is set by this lineage's own measurements - removing the sampled residual costs 0.116 and removing its cross-candidate correlation 0.051 of mean score - so the model changes and the rule that spends evaluations does not. What the siblings on this Parent tried lies on the other side of that boundary: they changed which candidates were eligible, how many were bred, how long the stall regime lasted, or reserved evaluations for a named group by quota, and the two reserved-evaluation arms were refuted precisely because overriding the ranking buys the candidates the single model had priced correctly. The number of predictive scales the model carries is the one thing no node in this lineage has ever changed, and it is the only thing this node changes.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent prices every member of its fresh 160-member pool with one global accepted-only count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto Gaussian process that has exactly one location and one scale: the running mean and population SD of the whole accepted archive. In its own receipts that one scale is small and shrinking because the archive concentrates on one analogue series - on median_2 seed 0 the fitted score_scale runs 0.0468 at batch 1 to 0.0372 at batch 29 while the archive mean drifts 0.107 to 0.178 - and it is applied to a candidate sitting inside the incumbent series and to a candidate in a region the archive barely covers alike, so the model's uncertainty does not grow where its knowledge stops. The consequences are recorded on this exact allocator. Chemistry away from the archive is systematically under-bought: n-d527b3b4e2cb gave a second generator 24.86% of the supply and the posterior bought 231 of 4,350 evaluations from it, priced it below the graph arm in 433 of 435 batches with the posterior-mean gap widening 0.0257 / 0.1155 / 0.1498 across session thirds, and 292 of 435 batches bought none; n-36afb69ebdd1 showed a 640-member field still bought lengthened multi-call products at 1.072% per pooled candidate against 1.738% for single-call candidates. Forcing the purchase does not recover the gain, because an override buys what the single model priced correctly: n-df6911ea1fe2 realized 870 of 870 reserved picks and its forced group converted at parent-beat 0.0989, survivor 0.4977 and incumbent-improvement 0.0299 against free picks at 0.1552 / 0.8319 / 0.0592, and n-82195b802723 converted its archive-far reservation at 0.000503 per evaluation against 0.001243 for the near half while the inherited rule's own far-half choices were the best stratum at 0.001767, panel -0.031639. The one decisive event in that whole class was under-predicted by 0.271 at a posterior SD of 0.013, a roughly twenty-sigma miss, so the binding defect is the scale and cross-chemotype calibration of the posterior rather than its ranking (h-95936ff259407586, h-8f75b2df9443d3af, h-b2785e70f134cc20). No parameter of the present selector gives the model a second scale, and the Anchor's own stall-time top-forty eligibility selects on exactly this posterior mean, so the mis-scaled prices also decide which candidates are eligible while the search is stuck.

sources.finding: Standard BO assumes uniform smoothness, so in multi-regime problems such as drug discovery across heterogeneous scaffolds a single GP oversmooths sharp transitions or injects spurious noise and miscalibrates uncertainty. RAMBO replaces it with a Dirichlet-process mixture of GPs, each regime an independent GP with locally fitted hyperparameters, and infers regimes online by collapsed Gibbs sampling that analytically marginalizes the latent functions. Read in full: the assignment conditional is a CRP prior times a likelihood, the member count n_{k,-i} times that regime's GP posterior predictive density of the record's label for an existing regime and the concentration alpha times a prior-predictive average for a new regime; the concentration follows the log-sqrt schedule alpha_t = alpha_0*sqrt(t)/log(t+e) with alpha_0 = 0.2; the predictive variance is the moment-matched mixture variance sum_k w_k(sigma_k^2 + mu_k^2) - mu_mix^2, whose two parts are the intra-regime average GP variance and the inter-regime disagreement among regime means, with spatial weights w_k(x) proportional to (n_k/(n+alpha))/sigma_k(x) and a new or empty regime priced at weight alpha/(n+alpha) with prior mean and prior variance k(x,x)+sigma_n^2; the reported acquisition is a weight-weighted sum of per-regime expected improvement. Reported gains over SGP, TuRBO, SAASBO, BAxUS and others on synthetic tasks, a 12-dimensional molecular conformer problem and a 50-dimensional virtual-screening problem over PCA-reduced 2048-bit Morgan fingerprints.

finding_summary.headline: The regime mixture ran and moved real purchases, but it de-priced the incumbent's own minority regime; panel fell 0.137
finding_summary.insights:
The regime split is inferable at this budget and its purchases are real, so the open question of this route is now answered in the negative at the layer that matters. What the campaign did not know is why: the failure is in the weighting principle, not in the split. The component weight is proportional to membership mass over the component's own predictive SD, exactly as the source method specifies, which makes the predictive mean a popularity-weighted average. On a maximization problem the best-known chemistry is almost always the smallest regime, so the rule systematically discounts precisely the candidates nearest the incumbent: the incumbent's component held 8 to 63 per cent of the archive in the active cells and under 38 per cent in seven of the eight, 82 to 100 per cent of pool members were dominated by the largest component, and in all three sitagliptin_mpo cells the incumbent's own component was the largest in just 1 of 29 batches, and the single GP's top-ten candidates were marked down by 0.05 to 0.24 while the pool mean barely moved. For the same reason the predicted far-field uncertainty growth never appeared: with the kernel fixed and only location and scale allowed to differ per component - the deliberate deviation from the source method, which fits per-regime amplitude and lengthscale - the only new variance term is disagreement between component means, and that is largest near the archive where the components actually overlap, not out where knowledge stops. So the far/near SD ratio fell in every single batch. This rules out a specific and previously plausible hypothesis: giving the predictor more locations and scales, with the covariance shape held fixed, does not produce comparable cross-chemotype uncertainty, and the archive-distance calibration defect this lineage has documented for three windows cannot be repaired by partitioning labels alone.

Two things are narrowed rather than closed. First, the premise that recalibration would not convert was never tested here, because calibration did not improve in the registered sense; the one part that did improve, held-out-component interval coverage closer to nominal in 11 of 12 sessions, coexisted with worse standardized error, which says the mixture widened intervals without putting the width where the error is. A predictor that makes uncertainty grow with archive distance has to change the covariance - per-regime amplitude or lengthscale, or an explicit distance-dependent prior variance - not the number of means. Second, the price-gap observable did move as predicted wherever the partition split, so the mechanism can be made to compress the near-versus-far price gap; it simply bought worse chemistry while doing it.

On method, two limitations are now measured on this node's own trajectories. The surrogate's ranking agreed less with realized scores than the Parent's did: pooled chronological batch rank correlation between predicted and realized offspring scores fell to 0.42 from 0.52, and the number of batches where the surrogate beat the archive-mean baseline fell to 364 of 435 from 415, with the collapse concentrated in sitagliptin_mpo (3 to 8 of 29 batches against the Parent's 17 to 28) - the same objective where the mechanism was most active and the score loss most consistent across all three seeds. These are each node's own purchases on diverged archives, so the comparison is descriptive, but it points at the ranking model rather than at the proposal supply, and the remedy is a different ranking rule - one whose component weight reflects the probability that a component contains the maximizer, or a single model whose variance grows with distance - not a different concentration or component count. The second limitation is the search scheme, and it is inherited: the Molecular report finds that within a cell the search enumerates one substituent of one scaffold (twelve proposals at an identical 0.6559 differing only in an alkoxy or thioether arm; ten of another cell's top ten the same enaminone), that diversity lives across seeds rather than inside a session, and that there is no size regulator - the drd2_docking seed-1 cell grew mean SMILES length from 87 to 154 while its best sat at 0.0289 from evaluation 24 to 249 and ended on an MW-991 polyketal cage with 226 of 290 proposals carrying a ketal inherited from one starting-pool sugar. That combination is what turned one mispriced first batch into a 0.94 cell loss: the operator set has no deletion move and the archive rule prices no structural novelty, so a committed line cannot be abandoned. The methods that would remove this are a proposal operator with substructure deletion and intact-ring substitution, and a retention or acceptance rule that prices scaffold-level novelty against the accepted set - not a tuning of the surrogate.

Finally, a measurement lesson with teeth for this panel. In the 158 batches where the partition stayed at one component, the posterior differed from the Parent's by at most 5.8e-4, and that was still enough to flip at least one of the ten correlated Thompson picks in 34 of them (21.5 per cent); in multi-component batches picks moved in 258 of 277 (93.1 per cent). The deco_hop seed-0 departure cell lost 0.231 with an essentially Parent-identical posterior throughout. Single-cell deltas on this benchmark are therefore not attributable to a predictor change of this size, which is why the panel-level reading, robust to removing the two worst cells, is the only usable one here.
finding_summary.results:
The replacement executed in all fifteen cells and routed every selection: 300 oracle calls and 290 accepted proposals per cell, all 435 pools full at 160 members, zero posterior fallbacks, zero invalid or duplicate proposals, and the twenty Gibbs sweeps per announced batch completed in every batch with no time-budget hit. Cost was never the issue: regime inference took 1.8 to 5.1 seconds per session and the audit under 3 seconds, the slowest cell ran 193.6 wall seconds against the registered 1200-second bound and the 7200-second task timeout.

The partition was real but uneven. Two or more components with at least two members each appeared in 230 of 435 announced batches (52.9 per cent, a bare majority, so the registered degeneracy falsifier did not trigger), and up to nine components occurred, but the session-median occupied count reached two or more in only 8 of 15 sessions against the registered 12. The two flat-label objectives behaved exactly as the degenerate control: all three median_2 sessions never produced a second multi-member component, and across the 158 one-component batches the mixture posterior differed from the inherited single Gaussian process by at most 5.8e-4 in the mean and 1.2e-3 in the SD. The posterior was emphatically not inert where it did split: only 15 of 69,600 pool members agreed with the passive single-GP value to 1e-9, the ten picks differed from the passive inherited replay in 292 of 435 batches (67.1 per cent), and 1,606 of 4,350 accepted evaluations (36.9 per cent) were priced by a component other than the incumbent's, with no quota, mask override or reserved pick anywhere.

The registered uncertainty geometry came out backwards. The archive-far to archive-near predictive SD ratio was supposed to rise above the inherited model's roughly 1.7; instead it fell in 435 of 435 batches and 15 of 15 sessions (for example 0.98 against 1.72 on sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 and 1.01 against 1.56 on zaleplon_mpo seed 2), because the only new variance source, the inter-regime disagreement term, supplied a larger share of total variance in the archive-near half than in the archive-far half in every session (0.89 against 0.80 on sitagliptin_mpo seed 0). Overall predictive SD inflated by 1.0x to 2.0x, and fewer than a fifth of pool members were priced more confidently in 14 of 15 sessions against the registered 20 per cent floor. The pre-endpoint ablated-cluster audit, read before any score, produced 808 comparable held-out-component splits: the mixture's cluster-over-random standardized-error ratio fell below the single GP's on the same splits in only 3 of 15 sessions (12 measurable; median_2 unmeasurable because a single component cannot be ablated) and in 414 of 808 individual splits, against the registered 12 of 15. That is the registered calibration-direction falsifier, and it triggered. The one calibration reading that did improve is interval coverage: held-out-component 95 per cent coverage moved closer to nominal under the mixture in 11 of 12 measurable sessions and was never worse (0.76 against 0.50 on zaleplon_mpo seed 1). The regime split is inferable at this budget and its purchases are real, so the open question of this route is now answered in the negative at the layer that matters. What the campaign did not know is why: the failure is in the weighting principle, not in the split. The component weight is proportional to membership mass over the component's own predictive SD, exactly as the source method specifies, which makes the predictive mean a popularity-weighted average. On a maximization problem the best-known chemistry is almost always the smallest regime, so the rule systematically discounts precisely the candidates nearest the incumbent: the incumbent's component held 8 to 63 per cent of the archive in the active cells and under 38 per cent in seven of the eight, 82 to 100 per cent of pool members were dominated by the largest component, and in all three sitagliptin_mpo cells the incumbent's own component was the largest in just 1 of 29 batches, and the single GP's top-ten candidates were marked down by 0.05 to 0.24 while the pool mean barely moved. For the same reason the predicted far-field uncertainty growth never appeared: with the kernel fixed and only location and scale allowed to differ per component - the deliberate deviation from the source method, which fits per-regime amplitude and lengthscale - the only new variance term is disagreement between component means, and that is largest near the archive where the components actually overlap, not out where knowledge stops. So the far/near SD ratio fell in every single batch. This rules out a specific and previously plausible hypothesis: giving the predictor more locations and scales, with the covariance shape held fixed, does not produce comparable cross-chemotype uncertainty, and the archive-distance calibration defect this lineage has documented for three windows cannot be repaired by partitioning labels alone.

Two things are narrowed rather than closed. First, the premise that recalibration would not convert was never tested here, because calibration did not improve in the registered sense; the one part that did improve, held-out-component interval coverage closer to nominal in 11 of 12 sessions, coexisted with worse standardized error, which says the mixture widened intervals without putting the width where the error is. A predictor that makes uncertainty grow with archive distance has to change the covariance - per-regime amplitude or lengthscale, or an explicit distance-dependent prior variance - not the number of means. Second, the price-gap observable did move as predicted wherever the partition split, so the mechanism can be made to compress the near-versus-far price gap; it simply bought worse chemistry while doing it.

On method, two limitations are now measured on this node's own trajectories. The surrogate's ranking agreed less with realized scores than the Parent's did: pooled chronological batch rank correlation between predicted and realized offspring scores fell to 0.42 from 0.52, and the number of batches where the surrogate beat the archive-mean baseline fell to 364 of 435 from 415, with the collapse concentrated in sitagliptin_mpo (3 to 8 of 29 batches against the Parent's 17 to 28) - the same objective where the mechanism was most active and the score loss most consistent across all three seeds. These are each node's own purchases on diverged archives, so the comparison is descriptive, but it points at the ranking model rather than at the proposal supply, and the remedy is a different ranking rule - one whose component weight reflects the probability that a component contains the maximizer, or a single model whose variance grows with distance - not a different concentration or component count. The second limitation is the search scheme, and it is inherited: the Molecular report finds that within a cell the search enumerates one substituent of one scaffold (twelve proposals at an identical 0.6559 differing only in an alkoxy or thioether arm; ten of another cell's top ten the same enaminone), that diversity lives across seeds rather than inside a session, and that there is no size regulator - the drd2_docking seed-1 cell grew mean SMILES length from 87 to 154 while its best sat at 0.0289 from evaluation 24 to 249 and ended on an MW-991 polyketal cage with 226 of 290 proposals carrying a ketal inherited from one starting-pool sugar. The methods that would remove this are a proposal operator with substructure deletion and intact-ring substitution, and a retention or acceptance rule that prices scaffold-level novelty against the accepted set - not a tuning of the surrogate.

Finally, a measurement lesson with teeth for this panel. In the 158 batches where the partition stayed at one component, the posterior differed from the Parent's by at most 5.8e-4, and that was still enough to flip at least one of the ten correlated Thompson picks in 34 of them (21.5 per cent); in multi-component batches picks moved in 258 of 277 (93.1 per cent). The deco_hop seed-0 departure cell lost 0.231 with an essentially Parent-identical posterior throughout. Single-cell deltas on this benchmark are therefore not attributable to a predictor change of this size, which is why the panel-level reading, robust to removing the two worst cells, is the only usable one here.

molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the node proposed 4350 optimizer molecules (870 per task, 868-877 unique, zero RDKit-unparseable). The output is heavily cyclic and heavily aromatic: digest ring_closure_rate runs 0.8943-0.9851 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6506-0.9805, and mean ring count per molecule runs 3.09 to 6.70. What it never produces is just as consistent as what it does. Not one of the 4350 molecules carries a formal charge (digest charged_rate 0.0 on every task) or a single specified stereocentre (stereocentre_rate 0.0 on every task, and no '@' appears anywhere in the text), although its own best molecules routinely contain one to eleven unassigned sp3 centres. Not one carries a trifluoromethyl group; only 14 of 4350 carry any geminal difluoro carbon, and those are difluoro acetals. The saturated 1,4-diazacyclohexane ring appears zero times, piperidine 24 times and morpholine once; a basic nitrogen sits in a six-membered ring in only 5.7% of proposals, so the basicity its highest scorers depend on is reached instead through aminal N-C-N carbons and bridged NH. Against that, 44.3% of proposals carry at least one motif a chemist would reject outright: 1467 contain a four-membered ring and 851 a four-membered *aromatic* ring, 240 a peroxide, 141 an N-F bond, 117 an O-F bond, 106 an N-Cl or N-Br bond, 252 a bare thiol substituent and 20 an N-nitroso. The same census over the Parent's published trajectories gives 41.9%, so the strain-and-heteroatom habit belongs to the lineage, not to this intervention; what is specific to this node is the mass behaviour, which varies violently by cell.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Two things separate high from low. First, size: the bottom of the distribution is pool concatenation - CCOC(=O)c1ccc(O)c(-n2cc3c(c2-c2ccccc2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3NC(=O)C2CCN(C)CC2C(=O)Nc2ccc(OCc3cc(C)nc4ccccc34)cc2)c1 at 3.2e-69 and CC1OC(C)(c2ccc(O)c(-n3cc4c(c3-c3ccccc3)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n4C)c2)OC2C1OC1(C3OC(C)(C)OC3CO)OC(C)(C)OC21 at 1.5e-33 - while single atoms F and S sit near 1e-26 and the winners are all 23-27 heavy atoms. Second, fluorine on carbon: the cell whose top-20 averages 0.10 fluorines topped out lowest of the three, and the cells averaging 1.45 and 2.10 topped out higher. Across the whole set no carbon ever bears three fluorines, so the fluorine axis the gradient rewards is only ever climbed one C-F at a time, and 36 of the 870 SMILES spend their fluorine on nitrogen instead.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Zero of the 4350 optimizer molecules across all five objectives contain C(F)(F)F, and only 14 contain any C(F)(F) at all - every one of those a difluoro acetal, not a fluoroalkyl. Fluorine instead lands on heteroatoms: 141 molecules carry an N-F bond and 117 an O-F bond. In the objective where its own cells' top-20 fluorine count varied from 0.10 to 2.10 atoms, the low-fluorine cell also topped out lowest, so the generator was climbing a fluorine axis one C-F at a time and never reached a fluoroalkyl.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build a geminal polyfluoro carbon; it has no CF3 or CF2 unit in its vocabulary.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Candidate generation needs halogenation as a multi-atom group substitution that attaches a complete trihalomethyl or dihalomethylene unit to a carbon, not as independent single-atom halogen additions, and it needs a rule that refuses halogen attachment to nitrogen and oxygen. Both are composition-level operator changes and neither needs to know what is being optimized.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every per-objective digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0, and no '@', '[N+' or '[O-' appears anywhere in the 4350 proposals. Yet the molecules themselves are full of sp3 ring-fusion carbons: its best molecules carry two unassigned stereocentres in the smallest sets and up to eleven in the largest, and the amine-bearing chemotypes it scores best with would exist as cations at physiological pH.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot express stereochemistry or protonation state; it emits only neutral, configurationally unspecified SMILES.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The candidate representation and the mutation operators would need to carry stereo tags and formal charges as editable state, so that two molecules differing only in configuration or in ionisation are distinct candidates the surrogate can price separately. Today they are literally the same string, so no amount of surrogate improvement can discriminate them.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The saturated 1,4-diazacyclohexane ring appears zero times in 4350 proposals; piperidine appears 24 times and morpholine once, and a basic nitrogen sits in an unstrained six-membered ring in only 5.7% of molecules. Where basic nitrogen dominates the output, 27.2% of the molecules get it from an aminal N-C-N carbon, and the best-scoring molecule of its strongest cell, CCCc1c(SC)c(Br)c2c3[nH]c(F)c(c13)CC1CC2NCCN1CCC, carries its two nitrogens in a 7-membered bridged diamine rather than a stable ring. The Parent's own highest molecule reaches the same basicity through a hydrolytically labile cyclic aminal, so this is a lineage-wide habit.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator reaches basic nitrogen only through aminals and bridged NH, never through a canonical saturated amine ring.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set needs intact, chemically common saturated heterocycles available as insertable and interchangeable ring units, rather than reaching amine-containing rings by single atom and bond edits that happen to pass through N-C-N. This is a change to the structural move set, not to any objective-specific prior.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In one cell the mean SMILES length rose from 87 over the first fifty evaluations to 154 over evaluations 151-200 while the running best value sat unchanged at 0.0289 from evaluation 24 to evaluation 249; that cell averages 67.7 heavy atoms, MW 991, 11.0 rings and TPSA 180, with 226 of its 290 proposals carrying a ketal carbon inherited from one starting-pool sugar. In the two sibling cells that did improve on the same objective, mean SMILES length fell monotonically across the run (69 to 52, and 77 to 41). Across the whole node 24% to 59% of proposals exceed MW 600 in its two largest sets, and the largest single proposal is a 231-character SMILES.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no size regulator: when local improvement stalls it grows molecules by concatenating whole starting-pool structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Candidate generation needs a substructure-deletion move of the same weight as its growth moves, plus a size-aware acceptance rule so that a cell cannot settle into monotone mass increase. Trajectory-local size drift is observable without knowing the objective, so a generator can monitor and correct it task-agnostically.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of 4350 proposals, 1929 (44.3%) contain at least one of: a four-membered ring (1467), a four-membered ring perceived as aromatic (851), a peroxide (240), a bare thiol substituent (252), an N-F bond (141), an O-F bond (117), an N-Cl or N-Br bond (106) or an N-nitroso group (20). These are not confined to the discarded tail: the best molecule of one cell contains two aromatic four-membered rings and an N-F, and the best molecule of another contains an aryl hypofluorite. The same census over the Parent's published trajectories gives 41.9%, so the behaviour is inherited rather than introduced here.
transferable_gaps.gap: Roughly two in five proposals carry a motif no chemist would accept, concentrated in strained rings and heteroatom-heteroatom bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A valence-and-stability screen applied before the oracle call - rejecting halogen on N or O, O-O and N-N=O bonds, and ring closures below five atoms unless the operator deliberately asked for them - would remove this class without any reference to what is being scored, and would return the oracle budget it currently consumes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 151 of 4350 proposals (3.5%) have six or fewer heavy atoms, reaching 8.0% in one objective's set and 20 of 290 in a single cell. Single atoms and two-atom species appear as optimizer proposals in every one of the five sets: C, C=C, C#C, F, S, FF, FCl, Br, OOCl, OCO and FCS. In the sets with a real score range these are the exact bottom of the distribution, scoring 0.0.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator spends oracle calls on sub-molecular fragments it cannot have expected to score.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation operators need a heavy-atom floor, so that a deletion or ring-break move that would reduce a candidate below a minimum size is rejected and re-sampled rather than submitted. This is a precondition check on the candidate, independent of any score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In one cell twelve proposals share an identical score of 0.6559 and differ only in a single alkoxy or thioether arm on the same fused core (COc1c2c(C)c3c(Nc4cc5nc(c4)c4nc5c(F)cc4OC)nc(=O)oc3c1C2 against its propoxy and propylthio analogues). Elsewhere ten of a cell's top ten are the same enaminone differing by an ethyl or a ring carbonyl. Meanwhile the three seeds of a single objective converge on chemotypes with nothing in common - dihydropyrazoles against indole carboxamides, flat polyaza-aromatics against 700 Da xanthine conjugates - so the node's diversity lives entirely across cells and none of it inside one.
transferable_gaps.gap: Within a cell the search enumerates one substituent of one scaffold; scaffold change happens only between independent seeds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The acceptance or archive rule needs to price structural novelty against what the cell has already accepted, so that a proposal identical to an archived molecule except for one terminal group competes against genuinely new skeletons rather than being enumerated. A scaffold-level distance over the accepted set is computable without reference to the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
